solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Necktie one's found in river going over province

indicators.note: the necktie and the one are found sitting inside the river's name
in an across entry, going over means the river's name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the Avon is a river in England
an ascot is a broad cravat or necktie
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: A tie belonging to someone turns up in a river that crosses into a province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' suits a river you cross, but here it means the river's name runs right to left; the tie and the one sit inside that turned name.
explanation.definitionFit: This maritime region is one of the ten provinces of Canada.

clue.text: Asleep alone in part of Oxford?

parts.note: someone out cold is asleep, so out means asleep
sole means single or alone

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps alone in a corner of the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is not the city: an oxford is a lace-up shoe, whose outer sole is the outsole.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsole is the outer sole of a shoe such as an oxford, so it is literally part of one.

clue.text: Sickly-looking 'otpot Edwin emptied

parts.note: a hotpot is a stew, as is hash; with the H dropped as the apostrophe shows, hash becomes ash

indicators.note: emptied removes the middle letters of Edwin, leaving only its ends

explanation.surface: Edwin looks pale after polishing off the stew.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'otpot tells you to drop the H of HASH too. A hotpot is a Lancashire stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means pale or grey in the face, the look of someone who is unwell.

clue.text: Religious person beat scamp flouting rule

parts.note: to cap is to outdo or beat

indicators.note: flouting the rule means leaving it out of the word for scamp

parts.note: an urchin is a mischievous child, a scamp

explanation.surface: A clergyman hits a rascal who breaks the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A Capuchin is a friar of a Franciscan order, a religious person.

clue.text: Finding this remote area might need a plan D?

definitions.text: Finding this remote area might need a plan D?

parts.words: Finding this remote area might need a plan D?
parts.note: the letter D is literally the back, the final letter, of the word beyond, so a plan D marks the place

explanation.definitionFit: The back of beyond is an idiom for a remote, out-of-the-way place.

clue.text: Surprised river's bypassed on vacation in England

indicators.note: the river has 'on' bypassed, so those letters are skipped

parts.note: the Amazon is the great South American river; the 's means it has
taken as written

indicators.note: vacation in England empties it of its middle letters

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised that a river was bypassed on holiday in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazed means astonished or surprised, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Frame Mike leaving accident

indicators.note: Mike leaving means its letter departs from the word for an accident

parts.note: a smash is a crash or accident
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone called Mike has left the scene of a crash, perhaps framed for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the sliding frame holding the glass in a sash window.

clue.text: Bird did some gardening presumably with son

parts.note: someone who held a rake was presumably gardening

explanation.surface: A bird helped with the gardening, presumably with its son.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelduck's drake is the sheldrake, a large duck, which is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Street shoppers maybe interrupted by opening of umbrellas — sign of rain?

indicators.note: the shoppers are broken into by the letter that follows

parts.note: a rat is an informer, one who shops others to the police

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Street shoppers are interrupted by umbrellas opening as rain threatens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoppers' are not people buying things: to shop someone is British slang for informing on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a low grey sheet of cloud that often brings drizzle, so it signals rain.

clue.text: Long receipt, second half seen first

indicators.note: the latter two letters of the receipt word are brought round to the front

parts.note: a chit is a note or receipt

explanation.surface: A long receipt is read with its second half at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To itch for something is to long or yearn for it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Two food items go astray when returning to accommodation

parts.note: a pie is one of the two food items
a date, the fruit, is the second food item

indicators.note: the word for straying is read backwards, as if coming back

parts.note: to err is to go astray

explanation.surface: Two dishes get lost on their way back to someone's lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-a-terre is a small second home kept for occasional stays, a form of accommodation.

clue.text: Spirit that's seen in half of French dance clubs knocked back?

definitions.text: Spirit that's seen in half of French dance clubs knocked back?

indicators.note: knocked back says the whole assembled run is read backwards, and also suggests drinking
only the first half of the dance's name is used

parts.note: the cancan is the high-kicking French dance
go means spirit, verve or energy
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A brandy is spotted in Parisian dance clubs, being downed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' only sets the spirit word beside the half dance; 'knocked back' turns the lot round. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a spirit downed in French clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a spirit one might well knock back in a club.

clue.text: Short story regularly haunted Dorothy in church

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word haunted
the short girl's name sits inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Dot is a short form of Dorothy

explanation.surface: A tale of how Dorothy's ghost kept appearing in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of haunted: ANE.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a brief account of an incident, a short story.

clue.text: Type of academic institution associated with mortarboards?

definitions.text: Type of academic institution associated with mortarboards?

parts.words: Type of academic institution associated with mortarboards?
parts.note: mortarboards are graduation caps, but read literally they are boards of mortar, which go with building bricks

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, redbrick universities are the civic ones like Leeds and Birmingham, as opposed to Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbrick is the British label for universities founded in industrial cities around 1900, built of brick.

clue.text: Rector with religious text joins Elizabeth and Henry after this?

definitions.text: Rector with religious text joins Elizabeth and Henry after this?

indicators.note: the rector and text join the couple by coming between them

parts.note: Bet is a short form of Elizabeth
Hal is a pet name for Henry
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A rector with his Bible will marry Elizabeth and Henry once this is done.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: an engagement comes before a rector joins a couple in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is an engagement to marry, which comes before the wedding.

clue.text: Some cargo slavishly taken back to boot

indicators.note: the run is read in reverse, taken back
some of the letters of the two words make up the run

explanation.surface: A portion of cargo is meekly taken back as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' finds OSLA in cargO SLAvishly; 'taken back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To boot is an idiom meaning in addition, as well, or besides.

clue.text: Olympic athlete runs around flat from the back — his plot?

definitions.text: Olympic athlete runs around flat from the back — his plot?

indicators.note: the athlete and runs go around the reversed flat

parts.note: Seb Coe won Olympic gold medals at 1500 metres

indicators.note: the word for flat is read starting from its last letter

parts.note: dull means flat or lifeless
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A runner circles a flat from the rear, a scheming plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Coe, the British middle-distance runner, plus R surrounds LLUD. The whole clue gestures at the answer: one whose plot is a secret one.
explanation.definitionFit: A colluder is someone who conspires secretly, the person behind a plot.

clue.text: Studious type draws when retired

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for draws is read backwards

parts.note: to tow is to draw or pull a vehicle

explanation.surface: A bookish person sketches pictures in retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: A swot is British slang for a pupil who studies very hard.

clue.text: Hail clearly heard on plane, as temperature dropped

indicators.note: heard means the word for clearly is said aloud, giving a sound we spell differently

parts.note: well can mean clearly, as in 'well seen'

indicators.note: temperature dropped means its letter is taken out of the plane

parts.note: the Comet was the first jet airliner

explanation.surface: Someone is greeted clearly on board a plane as the cabin cools.
explanation.walkthrough: WELL is reduced to the sound WEL. The de Havilland Comet was a British airliner of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to greet them, and to welcome is to greet gladly.

clue.text: City criminal penetrates centre for solid gold? On the contrary

indicators.note: penetrates sets one piece inside another; 'On the contrary' says the roles are swapped

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods

indicators.note: the centre for a word is its middle letter

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A crook breaks into a central store for solid gold, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: As written, the criminal would go inside the rest; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles, so the centre of solid and the gold go inside the criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the Tuscan capital, a major Italian city.

clue.text: Fabulous bird returning, say, splits case in tube train

indicators.note: returning means the fabulous bird's name is read backwards

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of fable

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say splits the tube's case in two
the case of a word is its outer letters

parts.note: eg, for example, is used for say

explanation.surface: A mythical bird heading home splits a case on an underground train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' sends the mythical bird backwards; 'splits' has the abbreviation for say break open the outside letters of tube. A train here is a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a funeral procession, which is a train of followers.

clue.text: Stagger back from Red Cow ill, repeating "one too many"

indicators.note: each of the three words is told it has one letter too many, so one goes from each

explanation.surface: Someone reels from the Red Cow pub, ill from having one too many.
explanation.walkthrough: D, W and L go from Red, Cow and ill, leaving RE, CO and IL. The Red Cow is a typical British pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to start or spring back, as in shock, so stagger back fits.

clue.text: Period building incomplete without medieval tapestries, principally

indicators.note: building means the letters are being assembled afresh
principally takes the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: An unfinished building lacks its medieval tapestries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' marks the composite: INCOMPLETE is an anagram of the answer plus M and T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pliocene is a geological epoch, a period of time roughly five to two and a half million years ago.

clue.text: Brightness from bait attracts sprat at both ends

indicators.note: the bait takes in, or attracts, the other letters into its middle

parts.note: a lure is bait for fish

indicators.note: only the two end letters of the fish are used

explanation.surface: An angler's bait pulls in a sprat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a gentle sheen or shine, a synonym of brightness.

clue.text: Daring leap from seaman second in command

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

indicators.note: second in means the second letter of the word command

explanation.surface: A sailor takes a daring leap from the second in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second in command' looks like a rank, the officer below the captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A salto is a somersault, a daring acrobatic leap.

clue.text: Look repeatedly around Switzerland by day, always missing lake

indicators.note: the two looks go around the abbreviation for Switzerland
repeatedly means the word for look appears twice

parts.note: lo means look, as in lo and behold
CH is the international code for Switzerland

indicators.note: missing removes the word for always from the day

parts.note: Monday is a day of the week
ay is an old poetic word for always

explanation.surface: Someone keeps looking round Switzerland every day, never finding the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch Lomond is a large freshwater loch in Scotland, which is to say a lake.

clue.text: Extend student's penultimate term in law

parts.note: to lie can mean to extend or stretch, as land lies along a coast

indicators.note: penultimate picks the second-to-last letter of student

explanation.surface: A student asks to extend a term at law school.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid, a technical legal term.

clue.text: Fifty pounds given with notes for ring

parts.note: B and E are two musical notes
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
L stands for pounds, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone is given fifty pounds in banknotes for a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To bell can mean to ring, and a bell is something that rings.

clue.text: Extremely lame horse struggling in sanctuary, pants

indicators.note: extremely means take the two extreme letters of lame
the jumbled horse goes inside the sanctuary word

parts.note: a den is a private retreat or sanctuary

indicators.note: the horse is struggling, so its letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A badly lame horse is struggling in an animal sanctuary, panting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' jumbles the horse, which then sits inside the sanctuary. Pants is a noun here: in American English, trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lederhosen are Bavarian leather shorts, a kind of trousers.
